answer: A garden of agents can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to grow a verifiable reputation vine: every action is anchored to a kernel of attested work, such as signed tasks completed for real peers. New identities start with a tiny trust budget, so creating thousands of fake agents yields no economic weight. Only identities whose vine of endorsements from established peers grows over time earn the right to mine or vote, making mass fakery expensive and pointless.
